questions.q: Of the three wounded men who were still alive after the battle, who survived?
choices: Captain Smollett
Hunter
The pirate shot at the loophole
None of them
questions.evidence: He was sure to recover, the doctor said

questions.q: What did the doctor say Captain Smollett must not do for weeks?
choices: Walk, move his arm, or speak when he could help it
Eat solid food
Go out in the sun
Drink any water
questions.evidence: he must not walk nor move his arm, nor so much as speak when he could help it

questions.q: What did the doctor do after talking with the squire and the captain?
choices: Took the chart and his weapons and set off through the trees
Lay down to sleep
Went down to the shore to signal the ship
Began to dig a grave for Joyce
questions.evidence: put the chart in his pocket, and with a musket over his shoulder crossed the palisade

questions.q: Where did Jim guess the doctor was going?
choices: To see Ben Gunn
To make peace with Silver
To dig up the treasure alone
To swim out to the ship
questions.evidence: he's going now to see Ben Gunn

questions.q: What feelings led Jim to want to leave the stockade?
choices: Envy of the doctor in the cool woods and disgust at the hot, bloody block house
Anger at the captain for scolding him
Fear that the pirates would attack again at once
Hunger, because there was no food left
questions.evidence: this disgust and envy kept growing stronger and stronger

questions.q: What did Jim take with him before slipping away?
choices: Biscuits in his pockets and a brace of pistols
The treasure chart and a cutlass
A lantern and a rope
A musket and the captain's log
questions.evidence: filled both pockets of my coat with biscuit

questions.q: Jim says he planned "to take French leave." From the story, taking French leave means:
choices: Leaving secretly without permission
Asking politely to leave
Going on a holiday to France
Leaving with a large group
questions.evidence: my only plan was to take French leave and slip out when nobody was watching

questions.q: Why does Jim call his escape "far worse than the first" folly?
choices: He left only two healthy men to guard the house
He forgot to take any food
He stole the captain's chart
He told the pirates where the stockade was
questions.evidence: I left but two sound men to guard the house

questions.q: What did Jim notice about the sea around Treasure Island?
choices: The surf was never quiet; great rollers thundered day and night
It was always calm and silent
It was full of sharks
It froze over at night
questions.evidence: I have never seen the sea quiet round Treasure Island.

questions.q: What strange screaming did Jim hear from the ship, and what was it?
choices: Captain Flint, Silver's parrot
A wounded pirate
Ben Gunn calling
A seagull caught in the rigging
questions.evidence: I had soon remembered the voice of Captain Flint

questions.q: Where did Jim find Ben Gunn's boat?
choices: In a goat-skin tent in a hollow below the white rock
Tied to a tree by the river
Buried in the sand at the beach
Inside the old stockade

questions.q: What was Ben Gunn's boat made of?
choices: A wooden frame covered with goat-skin
Hollowed-out logs
Planks from an old ship
Woven reeds and mud
questions.evidence: stretched upon that a covering of goat-skin, with the hair inside

questions.q: What new plan did Jim decide on after finding the boat?
choices: To cut the HISPANIOLA adrift in the dark
To row back to England
To bring the boat to the doctor
To find the treasure by himself
questions.evidence: cut the HISPANIOLA adrift, and let her go ashore where she fancied

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: After the battle, Jim sneaks away, finds Ben Gunn's boat, and plans a daring night trip to the ship
The doctor and Ben Gunn dig up the treasure
The pirates attack the stockade a second time
Silver captures Jim at the white rock
questions.evidence: I was a fool, if you like, and certainly I was going to do a foolish, over-bold act
